assessment: The incumbent achieves intended coverage in 32/40 exports (80%), below 95%, with median handling of 17 rather than at most 12 minutes. Assignment changes and renames accompany all eight affected exports, suggesting unstable course interpretation without proving causation. The seven-minute median for unchanged-assignment centers limits any universal bottleneck account: routine exports can already require little handling. Replacement delivery greatly exceeds execution time, but waiting and active handling are distinct. Zero cross-center rows supports only the sampled cases; the split-course center was excluded.

openings.claim: Current instructor assignments may exclude courses intended for a historical week; renames may instead produce apparent omissions during name comparison.
openings.delta: Separate actual membership errors from label mismatches before choosing a correction.
openings.prediction: With weekly membership fixed independently, assignment changes alter exported membership if temporal selection is responsible; renames preserve membership but alter coordinator judgments if labels are responsible.
openings.probe: Compare fabricated unchanged, reassigned, and renamed courses in private staging, varying assignment and name separately. Obtain agreed expected membership and coordinator judgments. Preserve the documented CSV and concurrent attendance entry; share a six-day total budget with Z2 within existing hosting.
assumptions: Expected membership can be agreed independently of current labels.
Historical assignment availability and production correction feasibility remain unproven.

openings.claim: Does replacement handling mainly involve requesting and tracking delivery, or checking and spreadsheet work after delivery?
openings.delta: Identify active work separately from elapsed waiting before changing replacement access.
openings.prediction: Immediate availability reduces active minutes if delivery coordination dominates; comparable active effort persists if checking or importing dominates.
openings.probe: Use six coordinators' two short sessions with comparable fabricated CSV tasks. Counterbalance ordinary request handling and immediate availability; separately time requesting, checking, correction, download, and import. Retain private, center-scoped access, schema compatibility, concurrent attendance entry, and the shared budget.
assumptions: Shorter delivery delay alone establishes neither lower handling time nor better coverage.
